terms.definition: The enthalpy change that accompanies the formation of one mole of an ionic lattice from its gaseous ions under standard conditions.
terms.examiner: Formation of the lattice from gaseous ions, so it is exothermic. "One mole of gaseous ions" is the common wrong answer.

terms.definition: The enthalpy change when one mole of gaseous atoms is formed from the element in its standard state.
terms.examiner: For chlorine it is ½Cl₂(g) → Cl(g): one mole of atoms, half a mole of molecules.

terms.definition: The energy required to remove one electron from each atom in one mole of gaseous atoms to form one mole of gaseous 1+ ions.
terms.examiner: Gaseous atoms and gaseous ions: include the state symbols in the equation.

terms.definition: The enthalpy change when one electron is added to each atom in one mole of gaseous atoms to form one mole of gaseous 1– ions.
terms.examiner: The first is exothermic; the second is endothermic because the electron is repelled by the negative ion.

terms.definition: The enthalpy change when one mole of a solute dissolves completely in a solvent.
terms.examiner: ΔH(solution) = –lattice enthalpy + sum of the hydration enthalpies of the ions.

terms.definition: The enthalpy change when one mole of gaseous ions dissolves in water to form one mole of aqueous ions.
terms.examiner: More exothermic for smaller ions and for ions of higher charge, which attract water molecules more strongly.
